raw_response:
I am 45 years old, and I have farmed this land since I was 15, right after I finished middle school. My father taught me everything, and I learned the rest by watching what works in our village here in Quzhou. I have 3.5 mu, all in wheat-maize rotation. My family has six people, but my son and daughter-in-law work in a factory over in Handan, so they only come home for the busy planting and harvest seasons. That means me and my wife do the daily work, and we hire help only when we have to.

Right now it is spring, and my wheat is already in the ground from last October. I sowed an improved wheat variety — not the most expensive seed, but the same one my neighbor Old Wang used. He got a good yield last year, better than mine, so I copied him. I put 15 kg of seed per mu. For fertilizer, last year I got about 450 kg per mu of wheat, but this year I want to reach 480 kg. I bought compound fertilizer from the input dealer for the base dressing last fall, and now I will side-dress urea when the wheat is at jointing stage. Altogether I figure 16 kg of nitrogen per mu — that works out to about one 50 kg bag of urea for every 1.4 mu, plus the nitrogen in the compound fertilizer. For phosphorus I use 6 kg per mu, and potassium 3 kg per mu. I do not put more potassium because the dealer says our soil here has enough, and with only 3.5 mu, every extra bag is money I could use for something else.

I have my own well, so water is under my control. I already did the winter irrigation. Now I will water three more times: at jointing right about now, at booting next month, and once more at grain filling if the weather stays dry. That makes four times total for the wheat. For chemicals, I will spray herbicide once this spring to kill the winter weeds, and one fungicide spray later when the weather turns hot and humid. Two sprays total.

For the maize after wheat harvest in June: I plant hybrid maize, 2.5 kg of seed per mu. I hire my cousin's no-till planter — I pay him 40 yuan per mu — because after the wheat comes off in early June, I have to get the maize in fast before the season slips away. No-tillage saves me diesel and time. I put compound fertilizer in the row at planting, about 5 kg phosphorus and 3 kg potassium per mu, then I side-dress urea when the maize hits the big trumpet stage. Total nitrogen for maize is 18 kg per mu. I irrigate three times: once right after sowing if the soil is dry, once at jointing and tasseling, and once at filling. I spray herbicide once after sowing, and if I see corn borers like I did two years ago, I spray insecticide once — so two applications total.

I expect 480 kg per mu from wheat and 520 kg per mu from maize if the weather is normal. Last year a late frost hurt my wheat, so I am keeping my hopes realistic. With only 3.5 mu, every 50 kg bag of fertilizer is a real expense, and I calculate carefully before I buy. But I would rather spend a bit too much on fertilizer than risk losing yield. A bad harvest is a disaster for my family; wasting some fertilizer is just a cost I can handle. I watch what my neighbors do, and if everyone around me is putting similar amounts, I do the same. Change is risky, so I mostly stick to what I did last year, adjusting only a little when I saw something work on someone else's field.
